_note: Recipe lessons (data/recipes.json): each part is played by its event data/events/recipe_<who>.json, which sets the recipe's flag. Our own lines.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: You look thin, child. Are you eating proper meals up there?

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Two turnips and a carrot, cut big. Simmer them in stock and soy until a chopstick goes through. That's all there is to it.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: Learned a recipe: Turnip stew.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: Can I tell you a secret? The store's best sellers are the things I eat for lunch myself.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: Potatoes and an onion, a spoon of sugar, soy, and a lid on the pot. My grandmother swore by it.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: Learned a recipe: Potato stew.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: No time for lunch at the forge. I pour hot tea over rice and flake a fish on top. Done in a minute.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: Grill the fish first, mind. Raw fish in tea is a crime.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: Learned a recipe: Ochazuke.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: Vegetables are the worst. Except pumpkin, the way Mom does it.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: She cuts it in chunks and cooks it with soy and sugar till it's all soft. It tastes like a sweet! Don't tell her I said that.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: Learned a recipe: Pumpkin nimono.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: The radio crackles into a cooking hour. A warm voice talks through a milk pudding: milk and an egg, steamed gently, dark sugar on top.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: Learned a recipe: Milk pudding.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Have you been picking greens on the hill? Bracken, butterbur, the little horsetails by the paddies?

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Two handfuls, a batter thin as paper, and very hot oil. Don't crowd the pan, or they go soggy.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: Learned a recipe: Sansai tempura.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Mushrooms come up under the pines after rain. I fill my hat with them on the way home.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: A handful in the miso with a turnip or whatever's about. Warms you right down to the toes.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: Learned a recipe: Kinoko jiru.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: When I was a girl we picked mugwort along the lanes every spring. The smell of it still makes me young.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Pound it into the rice with the mochi, and it comes out green as a new leaf. Two of rice, one of mugwort.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: Learned a recipe: Kusa mochi.
